name: Why do drywall cracks frequently reappear in Denver homes, and how are they fixed?

mainEntity.name: Why do drywall cracks frequently reappear in Denver homes, and how are they fixed?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, seasonal shifts between dry winter heating and summer humidity cause normal home framing to expand and contract, producing recurring hairline cracks along drywall seams. Furthermore, localized expansive soils can cause minor foundation settling that puts stress on door frames and ceiling corners. To fix these permanently, a contractor scrapes out loose compound, applies fiberglass mesh or paper tape across the seam, and beds it in setting-type compound, which resists seasonal movement better than standard spackle.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver's dry climate shifts and expansive soils cause framing movement. Contractors fix reappearing cracks by taping seams with flexible compound rather than surface spackle.
